ucs.title: [LLM] Turla (Secret Blizzard) ComRAT v4 / PowerStallion bidirectional C2 via Gmail & OneDrive web interfaces
ucs.description: Hunts for PowerShell, WMI provider, and script-host processes initiating outbound traffic to legitimate Google / Microsoft cloud properties (Gmail web UI, OneDrive, Graph, Google Drive). This pair of behaviors uniquely characterises Turla's ComRAT v4 (Gmail web-mailbox C2) and PowerStallion (OneDrive REST C2) — both reverse the usual 'malware needs its own C2 domain' assumption by repurposing fully legitimate cloud services for command delivery and exfiltration.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.src) as src dc(Web.url) as url_variety from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.app IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wmiprvse.exe","rundll32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Web.dest="mail.google.com" OR Web.dest="gmail.com" OR Web.dest="www.googleapis.com" OR Web.dest="onedrive.live.com" OR Web.dest="graph.microsoft.com" OR Web.dest="docs.google.com" OR Web.dest="drive.google.com" OR Web.dest="api.onedrive.com") by host Web.user Web.app Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 3 AND NOT match(user,"(?i)\$$") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let CloudC2Hosts = dynamic(["mail.google.com","gmail.com","www.googleapis.com","onedrive.live.com","graph.microsoft.com","api.onedrive.com","docs.google.com","drive.google.com"]);
let SuspiciousProcs = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wmiprvse.exe","rundll32.exe","mshta.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","msbuild.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (SuspiciousProcs)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (CloudC2Hosts)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| summarize EventCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            CloudHosts = make_set(RemoteUrl, 25)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where EventCount >= 3            // ComRAT/PowerStallion poll the mailbox/OneDrive repeatedly
| order by FirstSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let CloudC2Domains = dynamic(["mail.google.com","gmail.com","googleapis.com","onedrive.live.com","graph.microsoft.com","docs.google.com","drive.google.com","api.onedrive.com"]);
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Name has_any (CloudC2Domains)
    | project DnsTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, ResolvedDomain = Name;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\powershell.exe", @"\pwsh.exe", @"\wmiprvse.exe", @"\rundll32.exe", @"\mshta.exe", @"\wscript.exe", @"\cscript.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner DnsHits on Computer
| where DnsTime between (TimeGenerated - 5m .. TimeGenerated + 5m)
| summarize EventCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine),
            CloudHosts = make_set(ResolvedDomain, 25)
            by Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName
| where EventCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Turla ComRAT/PowerStallion Cloud-Service C2 from Script Interpreter
id: 6a31f7d2-7c1a-4e22-9f3e-1c0d2e8b4c01
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell, WMI provider, and script-host processes initiating network connections to legitimate Gmail / OneDrive / Graph / Google Drive endpoints. Turla's ComRAT v4 uses the Gmail web UI as a bidirectional C2 channel and PowerStallion uses OneDrive — both are unusual for any non-browser process to contact.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/2020/05/26/no-game-over-winnti-group/
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/2019/05/29/turla-powershell-usage/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1102.002
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.g0010
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wmiprvse.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_dst:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - 'mail.google.com'
      - 'gmail.com'
      - 'www.googleapis.com'
      - 'onedrive.live.com'
      - 'graph.microsoft.com'
      - 'docs.google.com'
      - 'drive.google.com'
      - 'api.onedrive.com'
  condition: selection_img and selection_dst
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned Microsoft.Graph PowerShell SDK automation under known service accounts — baseline and allow-list.
  - User-driven OneDrive uploads via PowerShell tooling — interactive sessions, not WMI/rundll32.
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\wmiprvse.exe OR *\WmiPrvSE.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\RunDll32.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE OR *\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe) @DestinationHostname:(*mail.google.com OR *gmail.com OR *onedrive.live.com OR *graph.microsoft.com OR *docs.google.com OR *drive.google.com OR *api.onedrive.com OR *googleapis.com)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(^|\.)(mail\.google\.com|gmail\.com|onedrive\.live\.com|graph\.microsoft\.com|docs\.google\.com|drive\.google\.com|api\.onedrive\.com|googleapis\.com)$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|wmiprvse|rundll32|mshta|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count(as=callbacks))
| callbacks >= 3
ucs.rationale: Turla is one of the very few state actors with a documented, repeated reliance on the consumer web UIs of Gmail and OneDrive as C2 — ComRAT v4 (ESET, 2020) parses Gmail web inbox HTML for commands; PowerStallion (ESET, 2019) polls a OneDrive account via PowerShell. A non-browser process beaconing to mail.google.com or onedrive.live.com is, in practice, the Turla operator pattern — not generic OAut

ucs.title: [LLM] Turla LightNeuron Exchange Transport Agent persistence (DLL drop into Exchange + Install-TransportAgent)
ucs.description: Hunts the two-step LightNeuron install: (1) a non-Microsoft signed DLL written into the Exchange TransportRoles / V15\Bin directory, and (2) the Install-TransportAgent / Enable-TransportAgent PowerShell cmdlets being executed on a mail server. LightNeuron is, to public knowledge, the only mail-server backdoor that operates as a malicious Exchange Transport Agent — making this an extremely Turla-specific detection.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Install-TransportAgent*" OR Processes.process="*Enable-TransportAgent*" OR Processes.process="*New-TransportAgent*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval Detection="TransportAgent install cmdlet" | append [ | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" Filesystem.file_name="*.dll" (Filesystem.file_path="*\\TransportRoles\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Exchange Server\\V15\\Bin\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ExchSrvr\\*") NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("trustedinstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","MsExchangeSetup.exe","setup.exe","ServiceModelReg.exe") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | eval Detection="Non-MSFT DLL written to Exchange path" ] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let ExchangePaths = dynamic([@"\transportroles\", @"\exchange server\v15\bin\", @"\exchsrvr\"]);
let KnownInstallers = dynamic(["trustedinstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe","update.exe","servermanager.exe","msexchangesetup.exe","servicemodelreg.exe","wusa.exe"]);
union
(
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Install-TransportAgent","Enable-TransportAgent","New-TransportAgent")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Actor = AccountName,
              Detection = "TransportAgent install cmdlet",
              Evidence  = ProcessCommandLine,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName
),
(
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
    | extend PathLower = tolower(FolderPath)
    | where PathLower has_any (ExchangePaths)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownInstallers)
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Actor = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Detection = "Non-MSFT DLL written to Exchange path",
              Evidence  = strcat(FolderPath, FileName, " | sha256=", SHA256),
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let ExchangePaths = dynamic([@"\TransportRoles\", @"\Exchange Server\V15\Bin\", @"\ExchSrvr\"]);
let KnownInstallers = dynamic(["trustedinstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe","MsExchangeSetup.exe","ServiceModelReg.exe","wusa.exe"]);
union
(
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any (@"\powershell.exe", @"\pwsh.exe")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("Install-TransportAgent","Enable-TransportAgent","New-TransportAgent")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Actor = SubjectUserName,
              Detection = "TransportAgent install cmdlet",
              Evidence  = CommandLine,
              ParentImage = ParentProcessName
),
(
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFileExtension =~ "dll"
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (ExchangePaths)
    | where ActingProcessName !has_any (KnownInstallers)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Actor = ActorUsername,
              Detection = "Non-MSFT DLL written to Exchange path",
              Evidence  = strcat(TargetFilePath, " | sha256=", TargetFileSHA256),
              ParentImage = ActingProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*Install-TransportAgent* OR *install-transportagent* OR *Enable-TransportAgent* OR *New-TransportAgent*)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\TransportRoles\*.dll OR *\transportroles\*.dll OR *\Exchange\ Server\V15\Bin\*.dll OR *\ExchSrvr\*.dll) -@Image:(*\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\msiexec.exe OR *\MsExchangeSetup.exe OR *\setup.exe OR *\ServiceModelReg.exe))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/Install-TransportAgent|Enable-TransportAgent|New-TransportAgent/i) OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\(TransportRoles|Exchange Server\\V15\\Bin|ExchSrvr)\\.*\.dll$/i NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(trustedinstaller|msiexec|MsExchangeSetup|setup|ServiceModelReg)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, CommandLine], function=count(as=hits))
ucs.rationale: Documented by ESET in 2019 as Turla / Snake / Venomous Bear's preferred Exchange-server backdoor, LightNeuron is essentially unique in installing itself as a malicious Microsoft.Exchange.Data.Transport.RoutingAgent. The Install-TransportAgent cmdlet is almost never legitimately issued outside MSFT's own Exchange install/upgrade workflow, and a non-vendor-signed DLL appearing under TransportRoles\
